MEMORANDUM (privileged) - Redstone Manufacturing, Inc.: Proposed Appeals Settlement (Form 870-AD, 7/12/2024) v. Notice of Deficiency (1/18/2023) and our Submissions. To: Engagement Partner (J. Halstead). Case 58-2023-00417; TY 2019-2021. Deadline stated: September 10, 2024.

1. BOTTOM LINE
- Do not sign as drafted. The economics are better than the 47% headline on some issues but worse than our own position on transfer pricing (Issue 3) and R&E (Issue 2), and the document has errors, overbroad terms and structural risks.
- Corrected settlement total is $2,479,680, not $2,489,680. TY 2021 is stated as $724,364; its components sum to $714,364 ($45,864 + $682,500 - $14,000). The Exhibit D "$2,238,820 / 47.3%" reduction should be $2,248,820 (47.6%) of the $4,728,500 total.
- Our supplemental submission's ceiling was $1,602,058. Settlement exceeds it by $877,622 (Issue 2 $173,880 v. $0; Issue 3 $1,780,800 v. $1,359,750; Issue 4 $525,000 v. $242,308).
- Recommended: counter (or request a revised 870-AD) on Issue 3 and 3(d); delete or narrow 3(c) and 3(d); correct arithmetic; add QIP/bonus depreciation on Issue 4; confirm limitations and docket status first (Section 6). 

2. RECONCILIATION (tax deficiency, $)
Issue | Notice | Our 4/22/24 position | Settlement
1 DPAD (TY19) | 163,800 | 0 | 0
2 R&E (19-21) | 434,700 | 0 (alt. stated 89,775) | 173,880 (76,608 / 51,408 / 45,864)
3 s.482 | 2,719,500 | max 1,359,750 | 1,780,800 (531,300 / 567,000 / 682,500)
4 Facility | 767,307 | 242,308 | 525,000 (539,000 / -14,000)
5 Penalty | 643,193 | 0 | 0
Total | 4,728,500 | 1,602,058 | 2,479,680 (corrected)
By year the settlement is 607,908 / 1,157,408 / 714,364 (corrected). Exhibit D's by-year "original" figures (1,153,320 / 1,798,289 / 1,133,698) exclude the penalty and sum to $4,085,307, while the total row uses $4,728,500; the by-year reductions ($1,595,627) therefore do not foot to the $2,238,820 total. On tax alone, the corrected reduction is $1,605,627 (39.3%); the rest is the $643,193 penalty. Interest is excluded and will be material (s.6601 runs from unextended due dates, as the settlement says; the Notice wrongly said "as extended").

3. ISSUE ANALYSIS
Issue 1 - DPAD . Appeals "concedes in full" under Treas. Reg. 1.199-3(d). But s.199 was repealed for tax years beginning after 12/31/2017 (Pub. L. 115-97, s.13305); the RAR itself says so (III.A) yet computed on the merits (and cites s.199A, which is irrelevant to a C corporation). A calendar-2019 corporation has no DPAD; the whole $2,340,000 (tax $491,400) was unallowable, and the Notice only challenged $780,000. The cover letter also says Appeals reviewed "case law" and a "detailed revenue analysis"; our supplemental offered no new authority on Issue 1 and merely stood on the protest. The concession is therefore a windfall resting on a legal error, in a document that is "not a closing agreement" (870-AD s.1; signature page). Reopening is barred only absent fraud, concealment or misrepresentation of material fact, or mathematical mistake (s.3(a)); a legal error is not listed, but Counsel concurrence on a repealed provision is a reason to expect internal review. Treat the $163,800 as at risk, not banked. Our protest argued a repealed deduction; consider Circular 230 s.10.21 (advise client of the return error) and ss.10.22, 10.34.
Issue 2 - R&E. Appeals sustains 40% ($1,368,000 of $3,420,000; $456,000 / $420,000 / $492,000) with five-year amortization starting in the year incurred; arithmetic ties (Exh. A). Our alternative was 25% ($855,000) over three years. Our alt. "<=$89,775" does not reconcile: on our terms tax is about $61,425 (or $108,675 at five years). Legal footing: for 2019-2021 s.174(a) allowed current deduction; mandatory amortization began after 12/31/2021 (P.L. 115-97 s.13206). The Notice's recharacterization to s.263(a) with 5-year amortization "consistent with s.174(b)" is doctrinally weak (s.174(b) was an election to amortize from first benefit; costs of specific contract production are normally inventory/s.263A costs, not amortizable). Our supplemental also cites a "shrinking-back" rule at Treas. Reg. 1.174-2(a)(4) and McFerrin (5th Cir.) as support; shrinking-back is a s.41 concept (Treas. Reg. 1.41-4(b)(2)), and McFerrin is a s.41/174 refund case: verify before any reliance. Secondary effects (s.41 credit, FDII, s.163(j)) are not computed and are swept into the refund waiver (Section 4). Counter at 25-30% only if Issue 3 does not move.
Issue 3 - s.482 . Appeals' "35% across-the-board" is not what the numbers do: reductions are 33.4% / 35.7% / 34.3% (34.5% overall); 35% would give $2,470,000 / $2,730,000 / $3,217,500. The reduction is a compromise with no stated arm's-length range or point. The methodology is also inconsistent across documents: the RAR (tested party RC GmbH; GmbH margins 8.2% / 8.7% / 9.1% against an IQR of 2.5%-5.8%; adjusted to the 4.2% median) differs from Wellspring's workbook (tested party the U.S. parent; reported margins 3.1% / 2.8% / 2.5%; IQR 4.9-7.3 / 3.8-6.5 / 5.5-7.9; medians 6.0 / 5.2 / 6.5; recommended adjustments $1.57m / $1.41m / $2.57m = $5.55m). Settlement implies U.S. margins of 7.8% / 7.4% / 7.6%: above Q3 in TY19 (7.3%) and also in TY20 (7.4% v. 6.5%); the workbook's note that TY20 is "within IQR" is wrong. Settlement exceeds Wellspring's median by $2,930,000 ($615,300 tax). Intercompany sales conflict: RAR $38.0m/$42.0m/$49.5m v. workbook $54.2m/$58.7m/$64.3m. Applying the RAR's own margin gap to the RAR's sales yields roughly $1.5m / $1.9m / $2.4m, far below $3.8m / $4.2m / $4.95m, so the Notice adjustments themselves cannot be reproduced; request Examination's computation. Counter at $5.55m (Wellspring median) with a fallback no higher than Wellspring's $6.7m ($2.0m / $2.1m / $2.6m), and require the numbers to be re-run once the data conflicts are cured.
Issue 4 - Facility. The capitalized $2,600,000 and $2,800,000 deductible (1,600,000 undisputed + 1,200,000 conceded) match Engineering's own memo ($2.6m improvements; $2.8m repairs). So the result is favorable and should not be reopened. But: (a) the cover letter's description of the $1.2m conceded (HVAC maintenance, minor electrical, flooring) is the inverse of our supplemental, which proposed capitalizing only $1.2m (dust extraction) and deducting $2.6m; Appeals has effectively split the other way. (b) Depreciation uses a half-year convention; nonresidential real property uses the mid-month convention (s.168(d)(2)); March 2020 placement (CO 3/18/2020) gives 2.033%, i.e., about $52,858 for TY20 rather than $33,333 (about $4,100 less tax; TY21 about unchanged). (c) More important: interior improvements to nonresidential buildings (excluding enlargements, elevators and internal structural framework) are qualified improvement property: 15-year, bonus-eligible (CARES Act s.2307; s.168(e)(3)(E), (e)(6), (k)). The $1.4m clean-room enclosure, and perhaps parts of the electrical upgrade, may qualify for 100% bonus in 2020, worth roughly $280,000 net of the TY21 offset on the clean room alone. The loading dock is not QIP. Verify the framework exclusion and any election out; claim before signing, because s.3(c) would otherwise waive it. Scope facts conflict across the Notice (enlargement, new HVAC, roof replacement), RAR (HVAC $1.9m, dock $0.5m, roof/parking $1.6m), Engineering memo and our supplemental (HVAC $1.1m, floors $0.9m, electrical $0.6m, dust extraction $1.2m).
Issue 5 - Penalty. Withdrawn under s.6664(c) based on reliance on Wellspring and Crestview. This is generous: the RAR found no contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (study created in response to IDR 7), a one-page cost-plus policy, and a repair characterization contradicted by contractor records. Notice figures were inconsistent ($643,193 v. $697,361 computed; "net of applicable credits" unexplained; s.6662(d)(1)(B) misstated). The Group Manager's approval date on the RAR is blank (s.6751(b) written supervisory approval). If the settlement fails, a penalty on the settlement base would be about $461,160 (20% x $2,305,800) and these defects are our leverage. 

4. TERMS
- s.3(a) no-reopening: standard, but the form is not a s.7121 closing agreement (see Botany Worsted Mills v. United States, 278 U.S. 282 (1929)), so finality is weaker. Request one.
- s.3(c) refund waiver: far broader than the standard form (any item "directly or indirectly affected", whether or not identified) and omits the standard carve-out for carrybacks. It would waive QIP/bonus, s.41, FDII, s.163(j), foreign tax credit and NOL carryback claims for 2019-2021. Strike or limit to the adjusted items.
- s.3(d) CPM/MAP: binds Redstone to CPM-operating margin, bars advocating CUP, resale, cost plus or profit split, extends to s.901/904 computations, requires 30-day notice of any MAP filing and states CPM "shall serve as the basis" for the U.S. Competent Authority. That undermines our CUP/profit-split case, constrains Competent Authority, may prejudice MAP with Germany (which need not accept a U.S.-tested-party CPM, risking double tax), and could feed the APMA review of 2022+ (Wellspring: $522,984 extra tax 2022-24). Cover letter says the methodology "may inform" APMA. Delete or limit to the U.S. side; add express no-precedent language for later years; consider Rev. Proc. 2015-40 (simultaneous Appeals/Competent Authority) before signing (not independently verified here).
- Secondary adjustments (Treas. Reg. 1.482-1(g)(3)) are unaddressed; settle treatment.

5. DRAFTING. Because the form excepts "important mistake in mathematical calculation," correct the TY21 total, 47.3%, Exhibit D baseline, "35%" label and depreciation now.

6. PROCEDURAL AND LIMITATIONS (critical)
- The Notice's 90-day period ended April 18, 2023. A protest does not toll it; our protest (4/14/2023) cites s.6213(a) and "reserves" a Tax Court petition. Nothing in the file shows a petition. District Counsel's involvement suggests it may be docketed: confirm. If docketed, resolution is a stipulated decision, not a 870-AD, and the cover letter's offer of a "revised" notice and preserved petition rights is unsound. If not docketed, the Notice's amounts are assessable and Appeals' threat is meaningless.
- Assessment period: returns were filed 10/15/2020, 10/15/2021, 10/15/2022. Three-year periods end 10/15/2023, 2024, 2025, extended under s.6503(a) by the notice period plus 60 days (about 150 days), i.e., roughly March 2024 for TY19, March 2025 for TY20 and March 2026 for TY21 (my computation, not verified against statute text). TY19's assessment period may have expired before the offer unless Form 872 or an exception exists; none is in the file. If TY19 is barred, $607,908 of settlement deficiency should not be paid. An 870-AD waives the s.6212 restriction but does not extend limitations. Request the ASED history and any 872.

7. RECORD INCONSISTENCIES AND DISCLOSURE RISKS
- Protest and supplemental state that Wellspring prepared contemporaneous documentation for each year and (supplemental) that results are within the IQR; the RAR says the study was created during examination; the workbook shows searches in 2024 and reported margins below Q1 in all years. Protest says CUP primary; Notice says taxpayer used TNMM; RAR says cost-plus. Protest says Crestview/Wellspring advised; supplemental says Crestview advised on transfer pricing; protest also lists our firm as a tax adviser on the intercompany structure (conflict and witness issue for reasonable-cause reliance).
- Protest Exhibit F describes a 1/6/2020 engineering memo calling the work "maintenance"; the memo we hold is dated 4/3/2020, concedes $2.6m of improvements, and says it was prepared after the return and prompted by the IRS exam (impossible on its date; the exam began 3/2022). Our supplemental's facility facts do not match it. Examination began 3/14/2022 yet covers a TY21 return filed 10/15/2022.
- GmbH headcount (145 v. 67) and letterhead details differ across filings.
- Cover letter cites a "cost segregation analysis" we do not appear to have submitted.
These raise candor exposure (Circular 230 ss.10.22, 10.34(b); Ohio Prof. Cond. Rules 3.3, 4.1). Correct or clarify before any further submission.

8. NEXT STEPS
1. Confirm docket status and ASED (872s) this week; calendar 9/10/2024 and request an extension in writing.
2. Client call (Yoo, Bellingham) on: contemporaneous documentation facts; the 4/3/2020 memo; Issue 1 advice under s.10.21.
3. Have Wellspring reconcile sales, tested party and comparables; reproduce the Notice's s.482 computation.
4. Counter-proposal: Issue 3 $5.55m (fallback $6.7m); correct TY21 arithmetic and mid-month depreciation; add QIP/bonus; delete 3(d) and narrow 3(c); seek closing agreement; add no-precedent clause.
5. Obtain client's informed decision; evaluate Fast Track or Tax Court if Appeals refuses.

9. UNRESOLVED
Docket status; ASED/872; s.482 facts; QIP eligibility; Rev. Proc. 2015-40 effect; treaty article numbering. External law verified only for QIP; other authority cited from standard sources, unverified.
